properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 5 at 11:52AM MDT until September 5 at 2:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 1152 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the South Fork Burn Scar. Between 0.5 and 1.25 inches of
rain have fallen with the heaviest amounts on the northwest side of
the burn scar.  Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady
Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and
Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to
all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways. Impacts to
areas along the Rio Ruidoso may extend downstream of Ruidoso Downs.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms in and around the
South Fork Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flooding of areas in and around the South Fork Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Alto, Glencoe and Hollywood.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 5 at 8:41AM PDT until September 7 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties,
especially for south-facing beaches including the Lost Coast
Trail.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

Sunday afternoon. Surf up to 8 feet along west facing shores of

and west facing shores of the Big Island.

will make swimming dangerous.

and breaking waves due to elevated surf expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast
and Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...From 6 AM PDT Saturday through Tuesday evening.

currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially
pulling swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people
off beaches and rocks. Pooling of sea water is possible around

ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No
significant damage is expected.

officials.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 8 feet with local sets to 10 feet and dangerous
and potentially life threatening rip currents, largest on
south- facing shores.

Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Saturday to 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially
pulling swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore. Enhanced beach erosion will
occur. Flooding of sea water is likely, around the time of
high tide, over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such as
parking lots, beaches, and walkways. Areas most susceptible to
coastal flooding will include Avalon, Long Beach (Alamitos
Peninsula), and Oxnard to Malibu (including Point Mugu).

5pm on Saturday, 6.7 feet at 6pm on Sunday, 7 feet at 7pm on
Monday, and 7.2 feet at 8pm on Tuesday.

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks. Follow advice from local
officials. Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills-Lower Koyukuk Valley-Central
Interior-Dalton Highway Summits-Eielson AFB and Salcha-Two
Rivers-Upper Chena River Valley-White Mountains and High Terrain
South of the Yukon River-Upper Koyukuk Valley-Middle Yukon
Valley-Nenana-Chatanika River Valley-Fairbanks Metro Area

24 Hour rainfall totals across portions of the Western and Central
Interior have generally been between 0.75 and 1.25 inches due to
widespread moderate rainfall. This is a direct result of an
atmospheric river which continues to focus higher than normal levels
of moisture across the region.

Additional rainfall of .50 to as much as 1.50" inches will be
possible Friday evening through Saturday afternoon as a disturbance
aloft moves through and further interacts with the available
atmospheric moisture. Should this occur, 48 hours rainfall will
coincide with 5 to 10 year return intervals with locations receiving
the heaviest rainfall closer to 25 year return intervals.

While main stem rivers will be able to handle this extra volume of
water, some of the smaller feeder streams and rivers could see near
bankfull to minor flooding conditions. In addition increased stream
flows are expected for the next few days, so anyone planning
recreation activities on or along these waterways should exercise
extreme caution and be on the lookout for rapidly rising water
levels.
